extracted.intended_audience: NLP/ML researchers and practitioners evaluating generative LLMs on sequence-to-sequence tasks
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating large language models on sequence-to-sequence tasks (text summarisation, text simplification, grammatical error correction) using automatic metrics, human evaluation, and LLMs (e.g., GPT-4) as evaluators. Focus is on measuring alignment between metrics and human judgement and diagnosing benchmark quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Classic automatic evaluation metrics used to score model outputs (the paper contrasts these with human judgements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract notes that many popular automatic metrics score advanced models (e.g., ChatGPT) much more poorly compared to human reviewers, suggesting that classic automatic metrics are increasingly misaligned with human preferences for generative LLM outputs and may not keep up with current models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of human reviewers to assess model outputs across multiple metrics and tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human reviewers in the study consistently rate ChatGPT as outperforming many other popular models on the majority of metrics. Also, humans sometimes rate the gold reference as worse than the best model outputs, indicating problems with benchmark reference quality—so human evaluation should consider relative ranking and reference quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid evaluation (automatic + human)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine automatic metrics and human evaluation to obtain a more comprehensive assessment of model performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper performs a preliminary and hybrid evaluation using both automatic and human evaluation, implying that relying on a single type of evaluator (automatic or human) can miss important aspects of model quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using GPT-4 as an evaluator
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore whether GPT-4 (and similar LLMs) can act as automatic evaluators by ranking or scoring model outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors find that GPT-4 is capable of ranking models' outputs in a way which aligns reasonably closely to human judgement despite task-specific variations. However, alignment is lower for certain tasks (notably grammatical error correction), so LLM-based evaluation should be validated per task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with human judgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how well an evaluation metric (automatic metric or LLM-based evaluator) agrees with human rankings or scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key evaluation objective is ranking alignment with human judgement. The paper reports that GPT-4's rankings align reasonably closely to human judgement overall but that classic automatic metrics often diverge from human assessments; alignment varies by task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task-specific behavior and evaluation variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that evaluation metrics and evaluator alignment can vary across different sequence-to-sequence tasks (text summarisation, text simplification, grammatical error correction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study highlights task-specific variations: e.g., lower alignment between GPT-4 and humans in GEC. Evaluations should therefore be analysed separately per task rather than assuming uniform behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark / gold reference quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the quality of benchmark gold references, since poor-quality references can distort metric evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human reviewers rated the gold reference as much worse than the best models' outputs in the authors' experiments, indicating that many popular benchmarks may have low-quality references; evaluators should check reference quality and not treat gold references as infallible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to rank model outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether an evaluator (metric, human, or LLM) can produce a reliable ranking of candidate outputs from different models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper explicitly assesses ranking capability and reports that GPT-4 can rank outputs in a way that reasonably matches human rankings, suggesting ranking agreement is a useful criterion for evaluator utility.
